L19@P1: Colin Defant & Nathan Williams
L20@P1: Abstract Given a finite irreducible Coxeter group W with a fixed Coxeter element c, we define
L21@P1: the Coxeter pop-tsack torsing operator PopT : W → W by PopT (w) = w · πT (w)−1, where
L22@P1: πT (w) is the join in the noncrossing partition lattice NC(w, c) of the set of reflections lying
L23@P1: weakly below w in the absolute order. This definition serves as a “Bessis dual” version of the
L24@P1: first author’s notion of a Coxeter pop-stack sorting operator, which, in turn, generalizes the
L25@P1: pop-stack sorting map on symmetric groups. We show that if W is coincidental or of type D,
L26@P1: then the identity element of W is the unique periodic point of PopT and the maximum size
L27@P1: of a forward orbit of PopT is the Coxeter number h of W. In each of these types, we obtain a
L28@P1: natural lift from W to the dual braid monoid of W. We also prove that W is coincidental if
L29@P1: and only if it has a unique forward orbit of size h. For arbitrary W, we show that the forward
L30@P1: orbit of c−1 under PopT has size h and is isolated in the sense that none of the non-identity
L31@P1: elements of the orbit have preimages lying outside of the orbit.

L37@P1: i denotes the ith iterate of f. One of the primary aims of dynamical combinatorics is to understand the sizes of forward orbits of combinatorially-defined maps.
L38@P1: A rich source of combinatorial dynamical systems comes from the symmetric group
L39@P1: Sn, which is the group of permutations of the set [n] := {1, . . . , n}. For example, the
L40@P1: pop-stack sorting map is the function Pop : Sn → Sn that acts by reversing all of
L41@P1: the descending runs of a permutation while keeping different descending runs in the
L42@P1: same order relative to each other. This map, which originally appeared in an article by
L43@P1: Ungar concerning directions determined by points in the plane [28], has gained interest
L44@P1: in the past few years among enumerative combinatorialists [1, 5, 4, 20, 17, 18, 22].
L45@P1: See [19] and the references therein for several other dynamical systems arising from
L46@P1: sorting operators on permutations.
L47@P1: It is not difficult to show that the identity permutation e = 12 · · · n is the unique
L48@P1: fixed point of Pop : Sn → Sn and that every forward orbit of this map contains e.
